quest.title: A Day the Grand Temple Inscribed with Ages
quest.description: The Keepers of the Pillar Hall consider the contents of Zeitlind's suitcase to be relics, and have placed them throughout the Temple of Space. Istoria says that many people are still waiting for rescue in those same areas...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x60000, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: A Long Day in the Mountains: Chapter 1
chapter.title: Paradise

talks.objective: Find Zeitlind's lost belongings and liberate the areas

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... thank you. I'm really glad I met you at the end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. If anything, it feels like you got dragged into all this because of us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, "the end"? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I mean... ours were all pretty dangerous adventures. But I got to see so many incredible things.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That's not so bad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't just brush Paimon's question off like that.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Did I?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Istoria, we've basically freed all three areas. Most of the people are safe now, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And we even found everything Zeitlind lost.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you very much. I have to say, Nihilita's got quite the eye for people now that he's opened it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, your turn now! You mentioned a way to go up above before, and a price to go with it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bring it on! Paimon's not scared of a couple of adventures or a bit of Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! And what about Zeitlind? How are we supposed to send her back down now that she's done here?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I can explain all of that, but you should rest first. I'll go through everything in detail tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. But um, there's no bed here. Or food!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Such desires cease here. Think about it. You've been here all this time, but you are neither hungry nor tired.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Then what's Paimon supposed to do all day while we rest?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: This place is full of remarkable people from every age — speaking with them could be fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Alright, fine. But Paimon gets to sleep whenever she wants. Tired or not, Paimon's still sleeping on {NICKNAME}'s head!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, after you've rested a bit, could we talk? It's about what I mentioned earlier, the thing I needed time to think about.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Speak with me a while, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}. Paimon. Once you're feeling rested, come see me.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Are you feeling rested? Have you talked to everyone you wanted to?

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: Alright. Take your time.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: Zeitlind, calm down for a moment and hear me out. I have no wish to be disrespectful, or to speak out of blind hope.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: Your sister may still be alive.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: I saw her gravestone.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Her picture was right there.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: But... isn't it possible there's nothing buried within?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants that to be true, really. But isn't that kind of optimistic?

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: In the last letter she wrote me, my sister said she'd already decided to...

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: That farewell wasn't written as a final goodbye, was it?

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: She said she was going somewhere far away.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: She mentioned it to me before. She always wanted to travel the world before she got old.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: Hilda wasn't speaking figuratively. She really did leave the sanatorium and set off.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: She talked about that?

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: She was always so bright. She got along with people easily.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Then she probably never told you... that we were all that the other had.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Let me be honest. Let me be cold for a moment.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: If her leaving would've caused three or four people to grieve, that weight might've outweighed her sadness.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: But now it's only me. She knew I'd understand. That I would forgive her for it.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: It's not like that. You shouldn't think of it that way.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: You don't have to feel sorry for me. When we were kids, our parents were still around, and life was good. Those memories were enough to carry us forward.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: But growing up... The world gets hard.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: I've always been more introverted, and dealing with people at work really wears me out. I thought my sister, being so outgoing, would have it easier.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: But even she always looked exhausted once she grew up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: You two still have a future.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Oh. Then she probably never mentioned her fiance.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: He was just a good person. An ordinary one. Kind. Interesting. Sometimes I wish he hadn't been. If he'd been a bad man, things might've been easier.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: His family had a hereditary illness. Some strange disease — they never lived long.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: He'd joke about it sometimes, blame the Anemo Archon for planning Mondstadt too well, so even a family like his never faded out.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: One day, he said he was going to save the world, and then he left.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Save the world...

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Well, the world's still turning. So maybe, somewhere out there, in a place no one noticed, he really did.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: You know how you always say that if someone who lives forever can't love everyone and be loved back, the world would drown in sorrow?

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: I think you're right. Which means a short life isn't even allowed that much.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: He wanted to give his life to love. And it only hurt my sister more.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: So much that she was sent to a sanatorium in the mountains — this very place beneath our feet. A place steeped in curses.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: She never told me any of this. I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: And knowing all that, you still think she's alive?

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: I do. Because she did something here.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: And because of my fear, she was forced to live on.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: You have my respect, Istoria, you really do. But I think you've seen too much suffering across history.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Pain vast enough to drown the world... For someone as ordinary as me, even a small part of that is enough to bury an entire life.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: You can't truly understand my sister and I.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: So, how do I set foot on mortal earth once more? I'm just a short-lived little someone. Eternity isn't meant for me.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: *sigh*

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Mr. Istoria?

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: This place used to be completely cut off from the world above. There was no way in and no way out.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: But after Nihilita fell, Dex seems to have gained the ability to carry people of the living world between the Pillar Hall and the surface.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: Even so, it cannot return those who were chosen to come here. It is a Watcher in juvenile form, and that limitation is part of its nature.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You're saying Dex is the same kind of being as Nihilita?

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: If we want to go back down, there's only one way. We have to give up every memory we have, everything we know, and climb to the very top. In the past, that meant meeting the mistress. Now, it would be Melanta.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: So I can't go with you. But at least, let me see you off.

response.speaker: Istoria
response.text: Very well.
